As /u/Warpig-034 pointed out, Call of Duty has some great co-op modes throughout their series that are often overlooked. The series has historically done a very good job of supporting splitscreen as well.

I'm going to focus on the most accessible couch co-op games because those are the ones I've most enjoyed playing with my fiancee who is herself a casual gamer.

  • Diablo 3 (Ultimate Evil Edition) is my go-to "play with the girlfriend" game. It's accessible enough for a casual gamer to get into, and deep enough that you can waste lots of time coming back for more. Local co-op is especially well done, and supports simultaneous local and online play. Your loot is automatically divvied up for you, so you don't have to worry about who's grabbing the lion's share. The camera pans in/out for you when you get too far away or when you're close to one another.
  • Castle Crashers is a great local co-op staple along the same vein, with cartoony gameplay, a basic level up system, and lots of humor
  • Lord of the Rings: War in the North is a fantastic local co-op RPG, with a third person camera and a focus on good storyline.
  • 'Splosion Man takes a bit more skill, but it's a great comedic co-op game that requires you to work together to overcome obstacles with a boom
  • Monaco: What's Yours is Mine is a top-view infiltration game that has you play as a variety of characters to pull off the perfect heist.

Local co-op is super underdone for both consoles, they seem to be focussing on online play.
